rows.question: A man harassed a girl so much online that she attempted suicide.
rows.answer:

rows.question: Two groups fought each other in a market, disturbing the public.
rows.answer:
The facts appear to fit punishment for rioting under Section 147 of the IPC [1]. Section 147 makes it an offence for anyone who is guilty of rioting [1]. Whether it applies depends on what can be shown about the facts, especially any intention, knowledge or dishonesty the section requires.
Punishment: imprisonment (simple or rigorous) of up to two years, or a fine, or both [1].
See also Section 146 (Rioting) [3].

rows.question: Some people put up a hut on my land without permission and refuse to leave.
rows.answer:
The facts appear to fit Section 441 of the IPC (Criminal trespass) [2], which provides: Whoever enters into or upon property in the possession of another with intent to commit an offence or to intimidate, insult or annoy any person in possession of such property, or having lawfully entered into or upon such property, unlawfully remains there with intent thereby to intimidate, insult or annoy any such person, or with intent to commit an offence, is said to commit “criminal trespass”. [2]

rows.question: A man married a second woman without divorcing his first wife.
rows.answer:
The facts appear to fit marrying again during lifetime of husband or wife under Section 494 of the IPC [1]. Section 494 makes it an offence for anyone who, having a husband or wife living, marries in any case in which such marriage is void by reason of its taking place during the life of such husband or wife [1]. Whether it applies depends on what can be shown about the facts, especially any intention, knowledge or dishonesty the section requires.
Punishment: imprisonment (simple or rigorous) of up to seven years, and a fine [1].

rows.question: A doctor operated on the wrong leg because he did not check the file, and the patient later died.
rows.answer:
The facts appear to fit causing death by negligence under Section 304A of the IPC [1]. Section 304A makes it an offence for anyone who causes the death of any person by doing any rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide [1]. Whether it applies depends on what can be shown about the facts, especially any intention, knowledge or dishonesty the section requires.
Punishment: imprisonment (simple or rigorous) of up to two years, or a fine, or both [1].
See also Section 304B (Culpable homicide not amounting to murder) [2].

rows.question: A woman's in-laws harass her daily because she did not bring a motorcycle as dowry.
rows.answer:
The facts appear to fit Section 304B of the IPC (Dowry death) [2], which provides: (1) Where the death of a woman is caused by any burns or bodily injury or occurs otherwise than under normal circumstances within seven years of her marriage and it is shown that soon before her death she was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or any relative of her husband for, or in connection with, any demand for dowry, such death shall be called “dowry death”, and such husband or relative shall be deemed to have caused her death. … [2]

rows.question: A group of seven people stopped a bus on the highway and robbed all the passengers at gunpoint.
rows.answer:
The facts appear to fit Section 390 of the IPC (Robbery) [1], which provides: In all robbery there is either theft or extortion. When theft is robbery.—Theft is “robbery” if, in order to the committing of the theft, or in committing the theft, or in carrying away or attempting to carry away property obtained by the theft, the offender, for that end voluntarily causes or attempts to cause to any person death or hurt or wrongful restraint, or fear of instant death or of instant hurt, or of instant wrongful restraint. … [1]

rows.question: A man shot at a police team trying to arrest him; one officer was injured but survived.
rows.answer:
The facts appear to fit Section 307 of the IPC (Attempt to murder) [1], which provides: Whoever does any act with such intention or knowledge, and under such circumstances that, if he by that act caused death, he would be guilty of murder, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine; and if hurt is caused to any person by such act, the offender shall be liable either to imprisonment for life, or to such punishment as is hereinbefore mentioned. … [1]

rows.question: A woman borrowed her friend's gold bangles for a wedding and pawned them for herself.
rows.answer:
The facts appear to fit Section 378 of the IPC (Theft) [5], which provides: (k) Again, if A, having pawned his watch to Z, takes it out of Z's possession without Z's consent, not having paid what he borrowed on the watch, he commits theft, though the watch is his own property inasmuch as he takes it dishonestly. … [5]
Whether it applies depends on what can be shown about the facts, especially any intention, knowledge or dishonesty the section requires.

rows.question: My boss keeps making sexual comments and asks me for sexual favours.
rows.answer:
The facts appear to fit Section 354 of the IPC (Assault or criminal force to woman with intent to outrage her modesty) [2], which provides: Whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any woman, intending to outrage or knowing it to be likely that he will there by outrage her modesty, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than one year but which may extend to five years, and shall also be liable to fine. [2]

rows.question: My son was beaten by his school's watchman until he fractured his hand.
rows.answer:
The facts appear to fit punishment for voluntarily causing grievous hurt under Section 325 of the IPC [1]. Section 325 makes it an offence for anyone who, except in the case provided for by section 335, voluntarily causes grievous hurt [1]. Whether it applies depends on what can be shown about the facts, especially any intention, knowledge or dishonesty the section requires.
Punishment: imprisonment (simple or rigorous) of up to seven years, and a fine [1].
See also Section 323 (Punishment for voluntarily causing hurt) [2].

rows.question: Someone made a WhatsApp group post claiming my sister has an illegal affair, which is false.
rows.answer:
The facts appear to fit Section 499 of the IPC (Defamation) [1], which provides: Illustrations.— (a) A says— “Z is an honest man; he never stole B's watch”; intending to cause it to be believed that Z did steal B's watch. This is defamation, unless it fall within one of the exceptions. … [1]
Whether it applies depends on what can be shown about the facts, especially any intention, knowledge or dishonesty the section requires.
See also Section 500 (Punishment for defamation) [2].

rows.question: Masked men threatened a petrol pump attendant with a gun and emptied the cash box.
rows.answer:
The facts appear to fit punishment for criminal intimidation under Section 506 of the IPC [1]. Section 506 makes it an offence for anyone who commits the offence of criminal intimidation [1]. Whether it applies depends on what can be shown about the facts, especially any intention, knowledge or dishonesty the section requires.
Punishment: imprisonment (simple or rigorous) of up to two years, or a fine, or both [1].
See also Section 503 (Criminal intimidation) [5].

rows.question: Someone posing as an army officer sold me a 'second-hand car' that he did not own.
rows.answer:
The facts appear to fit cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property under Section 420 of the IPC [1]. Section 420 makes it an offence for anyone who cheats and thereby dishonestly induces the person deceived to deliver any property to any person, or to make, alter or destroy the whole or any part of a valuable security, or anything which is signed or sealed, and which is capable of being converted into a valuable security [1]. Whether it applies depends on what can be shown about the facts, especially any intention, knowledge or dishonesty the section requires.

rows.question: A bus driver raced another bus on a ghat road and the bus overturned, injuring many.
rows.answer:
The facts appear to fit rash driving or riding on a public way under Section 279 of the IPC [1]. Section 279 makes it an offence for anyone who drives any vehicle, or rides, on any public way in a manner so rash or negligent as to endanger human life, or to be likely to cause hurt or injury to any other person [1]. Whether it applies depends on what can be shown about the facts, especially any intention, knowledge or dishonesty the section requires.
Punishment: imprisonment (simple or rigorous) of up to six months, or a fine of up to one thousand rupees, or both [1].

rows.question: A man broke into my house at night and took cash.
rows.answer:
The facts appear to fit Section 446 of the IPC (House-breaking by night) [5], which provides: Whoever commits house-breaking after sunset and before sunrise, is said to commit “house-breaking by night”. [5]
Whether it applies depends on what can be shown about the facts, especially any intention, knowledge or dishonesty the section requires.
See also Section 445 (House-breaking) [6].
